ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of semicircle O with AB = 4. Points C and D are on the semicircle, and $OC \perp AB$. It is given that $\overset{\frown}{BD} = 2\overset{\frown}{CD}$. Point P is a moving point on OC. What is the minimum value of $BP + DP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect AD, PA, PD, OD. \\
$\because$ OC $\perp$ AB, OA = OB, \\
$\therefore$ PA = PB, $\angle$ COB = $90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\overset{\frown}{BD} = 2\overset{\frown}{CD}$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ DOB = $\frac{2}{3} \times 90^\circ = 60^\circ$, \\
$\because$ OD = OB, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ OBD is an equilateral triangle, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ ABD = $60^\circ$, \\
$\because$ AB is the diameter, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ ADB = $90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ AD = AB $\cdot \sin\angle$ ABD = $2\sqrt{3}$, \\
$\because$ PB + PD = PA + PD $\geq$ AD, \\
$\therefore$ PD + PB $\geq 2\sqrt{3}$, \\ 
$\therefore$ The minimum value of PD + PB is $\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of semicircle O with AB = 4. Points C and D are on the semicircle, and $OC \perp AB$. It is given that $\overset{\frown}{BD} = 2\overset{\frown}{CD}$. Point P is a moving point on OC. What is the minimum value of $BP + DP$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect AD, PA, PD, OD. \\
$\because$ OC $\perp$ AB, OA = OB, \\
$\therefore$ PA = PB, $\angle$ COB = $90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\overset{\frown}{BD} = 2\overset{\frown}{CD}$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ DOB = $\frac{2}{3} \times 90^\circ = 60^\circ$, \\
$\because$ OD = OB, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ OBD is an equilateral triangle, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ ABD = $60^\circ$, \\
$\because$ AB is the diameter, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ ADB = $90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ AD = AB $\cdot \sin\angle$ ABD = $2\sqrt{3}$, \\
$\because$ PB + PD = PA + PD $\geq$ AD, \\
$\therefore$ PD + PB $\geq 2\sqrt{3}$, \\
$\therefore$ The minimum value of PD + PB is $\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, AB is the horizontal diameter, O is at the midpoint of AB, and the semicircle is above AB; C is the top point of the semicircle, OC is vertical and perpendicular to AB; D is on the upper-right arc, located between C and B; P is on the vertical segment OC, and line segments PB, PD, etc. are drawn. Reasoning: Since AB=4, the radii OA=OB=2. Since OC is perpendicular to AB and passes through the circle center O, OC is the perpendicular bisector of AB; P is on OC, so PA=PB. Therefore BP+DP=PA+DP. The central angle ∠COB corresponding to arc CB is 90°, and because arc BD=2 arc CD, arcs CD and BD divide 90° in a 1:2 ratio, so ∠BOD=60°. Also OD=OB=2, so triangle OBD is an equilateral triangle, BD=2, and ∠ABD=60°. Since AB is the diameter of the semicircle, ∠ADB=90°. In right triangle ABD, AD=AB·sin∠ABD=4·sin60°=2√3. By the triangle inequality, PA+PD≥AD, therefore BP+DP=PA+PD≥2√3. And line AD intersects segment OC, so equality can be attained when P is this intersection point. Therefore the minimum value of BP+DP is 2√3.
